method_note: Each candidate names who sends it and what social risk the sender is outsourcing to the post.

candidates.title: Compliment Failed Successfully
candidates.suggested_text_hook: he had a compliment ready. his mouth chose weather.
candidates.raw_situation: Zuv rehearses something smooth, Aachu appears, and he panics into the least romantic sentence possible.
candidates.why_people_may_share: A girl sends it to the guy who tries to flirt and becomes a malfunctioning person. A guy sends it to confess, 'this is me, unfortunately.'
candidates.why_people_may_comment: People will confess their worst almost-flirts and awkward first-date lines.
candidates.likely_audience_reaction: Laugh, cringe, then soften because the failure proves he cared enough to panic.
candidates.visual_evidence: Kitchen or hallway: Zuv rehearsing with a spoon/phone reflection, Aachu enters, he blurts something painfully practical or weather-related while the prepared compliment dies in his face.

candidates.title: Not Waiting, Obviously
candidates.suggested_text_hook: i was not waiting for his text. i was just holding my phone emotionally.
candidates.raw_situation: New love stage: both are pretending not to wait for the other person's message, while their whole evening is built around that tiny notification.
candidates.why_people_may_share: Girls and guys can both send it as a confession without saying 'I miss you.'
candidates.why_people_may_comment: Comments become 'me refreshing WhatsApp' / 'the phone was in my hand for academic reasons.'
candidates.likely_audience_reaction: New-love recognition, mild embarrassment, high sendability.
candidates.visual_evidence: Split but same-room-feel composition: Aachu holding phone upside down while pretending to read; Zuv staring at a silent phone while pretending to work.

candidates.title: The Last Bite Court Case
candidates.suggested_text_hook: no one ate the last bite. it simply disappeared with witnesses.
candidates.raw_situation: One last bite is gone. Both are innocent. Both have evidence. The relationship briefly becomes a courtroom.
candidates.why_people_may_share: Married and live-in couples send it because food theft is a daily legal system.
candidates.why_people_may_comment: People will tag the partner who always says 'I only took a little.'
candidates.likely_audience_reaction: Instant everyday recognition; more funny than tender unless the payoff softens.
candidates.visual_evidence: Dining table, one plate with a missing last bite, two over-serious expressions, maybe a fork held like evidence.

engagement_rationale: The failed-compliment idea has a sender on both sides and a clean confession payload: 'I like you, but I am not smooth.'
distribution_risks: Texting/waiting ideas can feel familiar unless the visual is very specific.
Food-court jokes are commentable but may be less premium.
